newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian stocks firm, but new profit-taking expected.
newsitem.headline: Belgian stocks firm, but new profit-taking expected.

text.p: The Brussels bourse continued to consolidate on Thursday, closing up only slightly, but outperforming other European bourses, dealers said.
They were mixed on the effect on the bourse of the current political uncertainty in the Belgian government and most forecast that investors would take further profits.
"We're seeing investors cashing in on their gains but they'll soon start buying again and push the Bel-20 (index) up in coming weeks," said a trader.
Some saw the index reaching record levels by the New Year.
The Bel-20 edged up several points minutes before trading ended to close up 0.23 percent at 1,863.55.
Final volume was a firm 2.478 billion francs of Belgian shares, down from Wednesday's closing volume of 2.605 billion.
"Some investors had been cautious today because of the political uncertainty facing the government, but most shrugged off the events," said a dealer.

Parliament has asked the country's top court to further investigate allegations that deputy prime minister Elio di Rupo had sex with under-age boys. Di Rupo, who strongly denies the allegations, refuses to step down.

Steel maker Cockerill rose 3.45 percent to 120 francs, with dealers putting the gain down to a rediscovery by investors. Cockerill had been underpriced. "People are looking at shares that have been lagging behind the index," one said.
Newcomer bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet ended up 1.25 percent at 2,835 from its 2,675 franc issue price, gaining for the second day since the share started trading.
Chemical and drug share UCB fell 0.33 percent at 75,850 francs due to its high price tag and profit-taking, dealers said.
